ddl:
CREATE TABLE Card (
    Card_Artist VARCHAR(255),
    Card_Effect VARCHAR(255),
    Card_Endurance INTEGER,
    Card_ID INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    Card_Intelligence INTEGER,
    Card_Name VARCHAR(255),
    Card_Power INTEGER,
    Card_Type VARCHAR(255)
);

CREATE TABLE Card_Collection (
    Collection_ID INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    Collection_Name VARCHAR(255)
);

CREATE TABLE User (
    Email VARCHAR(255),
    Password VARCHAR(255),
    Phone INTEGER,
    User_ID INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    Username VARCHAR(255)
);

CREATE TABLE Card_Collection_Association (
    Card_ID INTEGER NOT NULL,
    Card_Rarity VARCHAR(255),
    Collection_ID INTEGER NOT NULL,
    Collection_Number INTEGER,
    PRIMARY KEY (Card_ID, Collection_ID),
    FOREIGN KEY (Card_ID) REFERENCES Card(Card_ID),
    FOREIGN KEY (Collection_ID) REFERENCES Card_Collection(Collection_ID)
);

CREATE TABLE User_Card_Exchange (
    Exchange_Time DATETIME,
    Exchanged_Card_ID INTEGER NOT NULL,
    User_1_ID INTEGER NOT NULL,
    User_2_ID INTEGER NOT NULL,
    PRIMARY KEY (User_1_ID, User_2_ID, Exchange_Time),
    FOREIGN KEY (Exchanged_Card_ID) REFERENCES Card(Card_ID),
    FOREIGN KEY (User_1_ID) REFERENCES User(User_ID),
    FOREIGN KEY (User_2_ID) REFERENCES User(User_ID)
);
gold_question:
Below is the database requirement description for a card management system: The system includes cards, card collections, and a user card exchange feature. Cards possess Attributes such as name, type, artist, effect, power, intelligence, and endurance, and can belong to one or more card collections. Users can manage personal information, including username, password, email, and phone number, and can exchange cards. Each exchange record includes the user IDs of both parties, exchange time, and the exchanged card ID. The database design of the system includes multiple entities such as "Card" (Card ID, Card Name, Card Type, Card Artist, Card Effect, Card Power, Card Intelligence, Card Endurance),
"Card Collection" (Collection ID, Collection Name),
"User" (User ID, Username, Password, Email, Phone Number), and relational tables "Card Collection Association" (Card ID, Collection ID, Collection Collection Number, Card Rarity) and "User Exchange Card" (User 1 ID, User 2 ID, Exchange Time, Exchanged Card ID). These tables are related through Foreign key to ensure the integrity of the system.
nl_text: The database name is rschema_0219, and it contains five tables. The first table, Card, has the following columns: Card_Artist, Card_Effect, Card_Endurance, Card_ID (primary key), Card_Intelligence, Card_Name, Card_Power, and Card_Type. The second table, Card_Collection, has the columns Collection_ID (primary key) and Collection_Name. The third table, User, has the columns Email, Password, Phone, User_ID (primary key), and Username. The fourth table, Card_Collection_Association, has the columns Card_ID (foreign key referencing Card), Card_Rarity, Collection_ID (foreign key referencing Card_Collection), Collection_Number, and primary key (Card_ID, Collection_ID). The fifth table, User_Card_Exchange, has the columns Exchange_Time, Exchanged_Card_ID (foreign key referencing Card), User_1_ID (foreign key referencing User), User_2_ID (foreign key referencing User), and primary key (User_1_ID, User_2_ID, Exchange_Time).
